title: Atomized token sampling & prefix-cache attribution pipeline
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: produce a lightweight, low-overhead pipeline that attributes per-token latency and marginal cost back to request-level accounting while isolating the delta introduced by prefix/KV cache hits vs misses. This ticket implements: 1) atomized token sampling inside the runtime loop (coordinated sampling choice to limit overhead), 2) a small tracing hook that emits compact per-sample micro-timings (microseconds) and cache-state markers, and 3) a downstream enrichment job that converts sampled traces into a token-level attribution stream consumable by billing, SLO, and dashboarding pipelines. The design must maintain SLOs (<=1% p99 latency regression) and keep added p95 CPU/GPU overhead minimal.
acceptance_criteria: Sampling hook integrated into runtime and toggleable via config with default sampling rate 0.5%
Traces include token index, subtoken id, start/stop micro-timestamps, cache-state (HIT|MISS|PREFETCH) and model-variant metadata
End-to-end pipeline produces an hourly aggregated dataset with per-token median/95th latency deltas attributed to cache-state
Dashboards show per-model and per-route cache-hit latency savings and a delta cost estimate for an example workload
Observed runtime overhead from hooks < 1% p95 token-serving latency increase in synthetic benchmark
Documentation and runbook for enabling/disabling sampling and for interpreting attribution outputs
technical_plan: Phase 1: Minimal tracing hook inside serving runtime: attach a single 64-bit sample id per request and, for sampled requests, emit compact events at token emission boundaries. Events are binary-encoded protobuf v2 with fields: sample_id, token_idx, emission_phase, ts_us, cache_flag, kv_key_hash, model_variant. Phase 2: Collector sidecar accepts UDP/batched TCP events, performs dedup+ordering, and enriches with route metadata. Phase 3: Enrichment job joins sampled traces with request-level metrics (token count, total latency) to compute per-token marginal contributions and cache-hit deltas. Phase 4: Export aggregated metrics to Prometheus-compatible time series (histograms) and to the billing ledger S3 path.
implementation_steps: Spike: implement a binary-sampled tracing hook in the local dev runtime and run microbenchmarks (owner: Miguel)
Add configuration flags: sampling_rate, max_samples_per_minute, emit_format (protobuf/json)
Collector: lightweight Go sidecar service in serving node to batch and compress events; deploy to test cluster
Enrichment job: Spark/Beam job prototype to join traces with request logs and compute attribution table
Dashboard: add Grafana panels for per-model token latency by cache-state and a daily billing delta chart
Docs & runbook: how to interpret outputs and how to disable sampling in emergency
testing_plan: Unit tests for encoding/decoding of sample events
Synthetic workload test: run 100k requests with known cache-hit distribution and validate attribution matches ground truth within 2%
Perf regression tests: before/after p95 latency and GPU utilization under 90th percentile load
Chaos test: simulate dropped events and validate enrichment job handles partial traces and marks uncertainty
End-to-end validation against production shadow traffic for 24 hours in 'observability-test' namespace
rollout_plan: 1) Merge tracing hook behind a feature flag; enable sampling in observability-test namespace at 0.1%. 2) Gradually increase sampling to 0.5% after 48h if no regressions. 3) Deploy collector and enrichment pipeline to staging, run 24h validation. 4) Release dashboards to Console-beta and make billing export available to finance on request. 5) After 2 weeks of stable signals, flip sampling default to 0.5% for all non-prod, keep prod at 0.1% until we have compute budget approval.
progress_updates: 2025-01-10: Spike complete. Hook prototype implemented in runtime branch 'feat/atomized-sampling'. Microbenchmark shows ~0.4% p95 latency delta at 1% sampling with protobuf binary encoding.
2025-01-15: Collector sidecar MVP reviewed with infra. Decided to use gRPC streaming with per-batch compression for reduced packet loss. Miguel to open PR for sidecar.
2025-01-20: Enrichment job prototype (Beam) produced initial attribution tables for synthetic dataset. Need to add logic to estimate uncertainty when traces incomplete.

2025-01-28: Performance review: hook overhead acceptable; product requested additional fields for route and billing tags — added to plan. Meeting scheduled with Finance on 2025-02-02 to align export format.
2025-02-03: QA blocked on secure log shipping credentials. Security requested short review; ticket will note to provide required proofs.
notes: Trade-off: higher sampling simplifies stats but increases overhead and storage. Default 0.5% chosen as balance for early rollout.
We intentionally avoid instrumenting every token to keep runtime overhead negligible; sampling must be statistically sound for tail estimates.
Consider later adding per-subtoken weight correction for BPE splits if attribution bias observed.
Finance wants a deterministic export schema; coordinate with billing team (cc: Elena Gruber) before enabling production exports.
